findings.text: Power wakelock control exposes lock and unlock operations keyed by textual name with optional timeout for lock. Both require block-suspend privilege and operate on a shared registry protected by a mutex, delegating activation and release to the wakeup-source layer and refreshing recency tracking.

Quality of service layer exposes aggregate reading plus target and flags update primitives, together with CPU latency and wakeup latency limit queries and latency request lifecycle operations for adding, updating, removing and testing activity. Latency updates that raise the aggregate additionally wake idle processors.

Power globals expose freezer timeout in milliseconds, filesystem freeze enable flag, trace enable flag and the main power workqueue pointer, plus early initialization routines for suspend state labels and hibernate size estimation derived from spare page count and total memory.

Lock requests reject callers lacking block-suspend privilege and reject empty names. The name extends to the first whitespace, an optional decimal nanosecond timeout may follow after blanks, and malformed timeout text is rejected. Nonzero timeouts are rounded up to milliseconds for timed activation while absent timeouts request indefinite stay-awake, with lookup failures propagated.

Registry search orders entries by prefix comparison over the supplied length plus a length check to enforce exact matches. A miss under lookup-only mode fails as invalid, a miss under create mode fails when a configured count limit is reached or on allocation or registration failures, otherwise a zeroed entry with duplicated name and registered wakeup source timestamped at creation is linked into ordering and recency structures and counted.

Unlock requests require the same privilege and a non-empty name after stripping a single trailing newline. The named entry must already exist, its wakeup source is relaxed, recency is refreshed and a garbage-collection step runs which in one build variant counts calls and schedules background work after a threshold and in the other variant does nothing.

Target aggregation returns a no-constraint value when empty, the smallest priority for minimum type and the largest for maximum type, warning and falling back to a default for unknown types. A default request value maps to the configured default, add and update insert into the ordered set while remove deletes, the stored target is refreshed, tracing records the transition, and callers learn whether notification was needed with notification issued only on change when a notifier chain exists.

Flags aggregation maintains the bitwise union of all member requests with zero representing emptiness. Removal recomputes the union from remaining members, addition stores the supplied value and unions it, update behaves as removal followed by addition, and the operation reports whether the effective union changed after tracing the transition.

Latency request handling ignores absent handles and negative values except for the designated default. Activity is defined by association with the latency constraint object, duplicate addition and operations on inactive handles warn and are ignored, updates with unchanged priority are skipped, and removal detaches then clears the entire handle.

Numeric control stores validate text before committing. Freezer timeout accepts base-ten unsigned values, filesystem freeze accepts only zero or one, trace enablement scans a decimal integer and coerces to boolean with a warning about clock disturbance when enabled, and any parse failure or out-of-range value leaves state unchanged and fails as invalid.

The power attribute collection always presents state and conditionally includes tracing, sleep controls, autosleep, wakelocks, sleep debugging, freezer timeout and filesystem freeze features according to build options, terminated to mark the end. A single group wraps this collection and the groups array adds a suspend-specific group when sleep support is present, also terminated.

Several wakelock helpers exist in paired active and inert build variants. The active forms manage a recency list, enforce a count limit, count creations and trigger deferred reclamation, while the inert forms accept the same parameters but perform no action and report no limit.

Hibernation size initialization has empty inline forms and real early-boot forms. The real reserved size scales spare page count by page size and the real image size scales total memory by a two-fifths fraction converted to bytes.

A dedicated wakelocks mutex serializes registry lookup and creation, wakeup-source activation or relaxation, recency updates and garbage-collection accounting across lock and unlock paths, held for the whole critical section and always released before returning.

A single quality-of-service spinlock with interrupt state preservation guards target list mutation and target refresh as well as flags list mutation and effective-union refresh. The latency read path also samples the aggregate under this lock while other limit queries use atomic single-copy reads without locking.

The stored target value is published and observed through single-copy atomic accessors that avoid tearing for concurrent readers, with locked updates refreshing the published value after recomputing the aggregate.

Hibernation header image info named swsusp_info begins with member uts for operating-system identity, then member version_code as thirty-two-bit version, then member num_physpages as unsigned long physical count, then member cpus as signed processor count, then members image_pages and pages and size as unsigned long image total and byte counts. The whole record is aligned to page size.

Snapshot I/O cursor named snapshot_handle holds member cur as current block index counting page-sized units, member buffer as pointer for the next transfer, and member sync_read as synchronization flag telling the caller that a bio-chain wait may be required after writing the next unit.

Constraint objects combine member list as ordered request set with members target_value and default_value and no_constraint_value, member type selecting minimum or maximum policy, and an optional notifier chain. Flags objects combine a membership list with member effective_flags caching the union of member bits.

Sysfs presentation uses a null-terminated pointer array for attributes, a group structure referencing that array, and a null-terminated group pointer array that optionally appends a sleep-specific group.
Each latency device pairs file operations for open, release, read, write and no-op seek with a misc device using dynamic minor allocation and a fixed textual name distinct per latency domain.

Wakelock entries progress from absent to present on first creation with registration and timestamping, remain present while lock and unlock operations refresh recency, move between active and relaxed wakeup states on lock versus unlock, and become eligible for deferred background reclamation once the collection counter passes its threshold.

Request handles start unassociated, become associated on addition or file open with a default or unconstrained value, stay associated across value updates, and return to cleared unassociated storage on removal or file release which also frees the backing allocation.

Power bring-up starts workqueues before any other step, tearing down the first queue if the second allocation fails. On success it initializes hibernation sizes and suspend labels, creates the power kobject, publishes sysfs groups, initializes timing support and finally initializes autosleep, aborting on the first failure.

Suspend test selection forms an ordered progression from no test through core, processors, platform, devices and freezer stages ending with an after-last sentinel. Named bounds expose the first and last real stages and the current level defaults to no test in the provided configuration.
Suspend label tables are seeded so that memory and idle variants are always advertised and the idle sleep variant is preset to allow idle suspend even when no platform suspend operations exist.

Unlock sysfs read shows the set of releasable holders without filtering to active ones, while write attempts to release the named holder and reports full input length on success or the underlying error otherwise.

Trace, freezer timeout, filesystem freeze and device-match sysfs nodes expose current values on read and validate and commit new values on write, with device-match read delegating to a dedicated formatter bounded by page size.

Power-off handling provides a work item that invokes the platform power-off routine, a sysrq handler that schedules that work on the first online processor, a key operation descriptor binding the handler with help and action text and boot enablement, and an early initializer registering the letter o key.

Latency device files allocate and bind a request on open and unbind and free it on release. Reads return the current aggregate as a fixed-size integer, writes accept either a binary integer image or hexadecimal text and then update the bound request, with wakeup writes rejecting negatives while latency writes route through shared validation that silently ignores invalid values.

Latency device initialization registers the primary device and, when system-wakeup quality support is built in, registers the secondary wakeup device, unwinding the first registration if the second fails and reporting errors.

Architecture header helpers complete initialization by saving with a bounded size derived from system identity size plus a small constant, and validate images by restoring and reporting architecture-specific mismatch through a descriptive outcome.
Enabling resume tracing perturbs wall-clock time across resume and requires manual correction afterwards, a side effect explicitly warned about at enable time.
Unprivileged wakelock access and malformed control text fail without side effects, ensuring that permission and validation failures leave registry, timeout, freeze and trace state unchanged.

Misuse such as duplicate addition, updates or removals of unknown handles, and aggregation over an unknown policy triggers a warning path while preserving existing state and falling back to safe defaults where defined.

The two latency write paths differ in negative handling: wakeup writes explicitly reject negatives as invalid while latency writes depend on shared validation that quietly discards invalid values yet still reports full input length.
Reclamation is deferred until a monotonic counter exceeds its maximum, so entries remain present between unlock and background work execution and depend on workqueue progress for actual freeing.
Power-off work is funneled to the first online processor to serialize shutdown with boot-processor context rather than running on the arbitrary caller.

Snapshot feature and compression selectors use zero for the dummy LZO selector, one for platform mode, two for no-compression mode, four for CRC mode, eight for hardware signature, and sixteen for the LZ4 algorithm selector.
Spare and I/O page counts represent one mebibyte and four mebibytes respectively converted to pages by shifting for page size.
Maximum architecture header size equals the size of the system identity record plus four bytes.
Generated power attributes use octal six four four for read-write nodes and read-only-for-all mask for read-only nodes, with names and callbacks derived from the base name.

Freezer timeout defaults to twenty seconds expressed in milliseconds, current sleep alias maps to the suspend-on state, high-memory page count helper reports zero in this build, and test level defaults to the first stage representing no test with the last real stage being the freezer test.
Latency misc devices use dynamic minor allocation with fixed names cpu_dma_latency for the DMA latency domain and cpu_wakeup_latency for the wakeup domain.
Sysrq power-off binds letter o with help text poweroff(o) and action text Power Off and boot enable mask.
Power workqueues use fixed names pm for the unbound queue and pm_fs_sync for the ordered filesystem-sync queue.
